cohort: Participants were 258 women undergoing emergency cesarean section deliveries at Karamara Hospital in the Somali region of Eastern Ethiopia.
finding: A decision-to-delivery interval (DDI) of more than 30 minutes was not associated with poor composite perinatal outcome compared to DDI of 30 minutes or less, though meconium aspiration syndrome was higher in the DDI <=30 min group.
mod_finding: The study indicated that for emergency cesarean sections, a decision-to-delivery interval exceeding 30 minutes was not linked to a higher risk of poor overall perinatal outcomes.
cross-section timing: Outcomes were observed immediately following emergency cesarean section deliveries.
